would it be better to cache the value and update it via a
PropertiesChanged signal instead of querying it on each entry?

Addressed. I have replaced per-entry SelPolicy D-Bus lookups with a cached policy in Manager. The cache is initialized once and updated via PropertiesChanged on xyz.openbmc_project.Logging.Settings, so createEntry now uses cachedSelPolicy and avoids hot-path D-Bus calls.

I'm not a fan of this term.  It's an IPMI term that isn't used anywhere else in the logging codebase.

I probably won't review much more until a common term is substituted.

Agreed, SEL is IPMI-specific and not a good generic term here. I have updated the commit message and wording in this series to use common logging terminology (log policy and log entries) instead of SEL, so it aligns with the rest of phosphor-logging.
I couldn't seem to find the commit that adds these in PDI. Can you point me to it?

These strings come from the existing Policy enum on xyz.openbmc_project.Logging.Settings in phosphor-dbus-interfaces (Linear and Circular). For this series, the PDI dependency used in CI is commit 4c95fecf0e84305a561f18906103cd152a3cb56b, which includes the Logging Settings interface used by this change.
didn't quite finish the review, will pick up after the holidays
seem unrelated
Agreed. That rename was unrelated to the log-policy change, so I reverted it and kept the original constructor argument style in elog_entry.hpp
This has been working fine for years for as far as I know.  why the changes?

Agreed. The default severity initialization in the minimal constructor was unnecessary for this series and could change long-standing behavior, so I removed it. The minimal constructor is back to id-only initialization in elog_entry.hpp, matching prior behavior.
the settings service name and object path are already hardcoded elsewhere in this file (and you are too below), so you may as well just hardcode here.

Makes sense. I consolidated the settings service/object/interface/property strings as shared file-level constants and reused them across all call sites, including this one and the existing QuiesceOnHwError path.
you would add the interface to the default settings config for all systems so everyone would have this interface and not see this message?

Good point. I removed the noisy “interface not found” info path and now silently fall back to Circular policy when Logging.Settings is absent, so platforms without that interface continue to work without log spam.
Please also update the main README with the new functionality.
why did you change this? I don't see why it's related.

is rolling over a worry?

this won't throw, so you can just make the match a normal member of the class and create it in the constructor.

same comment about nested try/catches as above.
in general you want to create the match before reading the property so you don't miss a window, but with my comment above that won't be an issue.

it's a match, not a callback.
